title: Personal Checking: mortgage principal in the Private Client Checking conversion test
content:
## Scope

This rule applies when an owner asks to convert a Personal Checking account to Private Client Checking and the Relationship Balance is tested against the Private Client entry requirement. It states how the owner's PCB mortgage enters that test.

## Formal clauses

1. **The target tier counts mortgage principal.** For this test, the target tier's treatment of mortgage principal is the one used, and that treatment is **Yes**: Private Client Checking counts outstanding PCB mortgage principal toward the Relationship Balance.
2. **What is counted.** Because the target tier counts mortgage principal, the principal balance of the owner's mortgage loan in each of the statuses active, delinquent and forbearance is part of the Relationship Balance, whatever tier the account is on before the conversion.

## Counted statuses

| Owner's mortgage loan status | Principal counted in the conversion test |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Delinquent | Yes |
| Forbearance | Yes |
| Any other status | No |

## Worked cases (hypothetical owners)

- An owner on Everyday Checking asks to convert to Private Client Checking and has an active mortgage with 160000.00 USD of principal. Because the target tier counts mortgage principal, the 160000.00 USD enters the test, even though the account's current tier is not the one whose treatment applies here.
- An owner's mortgage is in forbearance with 95000.00 USD of principal. Forbearance is counted, so 95000.00 USD enters the test.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "the account's current tier decides whether the mortgage counts". **Correct basis:** for this test the target tier's treatment applies, and it counts mortgage principal.
